patch_description: The current code runs a single greedy pass with random sampling, so the result varies a lot and often gets stuck in a bad local ordering. Two improvements: (1) run many greedy restarts with different random starting transactions and keep the best schedule found, and (2) add a cheap local search (adjacent-swap improvement) on the best schedule to squeeze out further makespan reductions. Since greedy construction is fast (only ~num_samples cost evaluations per step), doing many restarts is affordable and directly improves expected makespan. The swap-based local search exploits the fact that swapping two adjacent transactions in the sequence only changes conflict-induced delays locally, so small perturbations can yield meaningful makespan reductions. We keep the original greedy as a fallback structure but wrap it in a restart loop and polish with local search.
